To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ImageNet dataset is not special in any significant way, and that the success of the features learnt by training on ImageNet is due to the large number of examples, the large number of classes, the large number and balance of images-per-class, and the fine grained nature of the classes.

1) the number of classes is more important than the number of examples; 2) the amount of fine grained data is less important than the amount of coarse grained data; and 3) the balance between images-per class and classes is less important than either.

the number of examples, the number of classes and the balance between the number of images-per-class and number of classes do not have a significant effect on the transfer performance of ImageNet-trained models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: What makes ImageNet good?
the question of how much of the success of ImageNet is due to the data itself, and how much is due to the particular training procedure used to train the models
the following questions: What makes the ImageNet dataset good for transfer learning?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ImageNet has the right amount of data and the right amount of classes, but it is not the balance between images-per class and classes, or the fine and coarse graining of the classes that makes the difference.
ImageNet is a good dataset for transfer learning because it is a very large, balanced and diverse dataset, with a good mix of fine and coarse classes.
the ImageNet dataset is good for transfer learning because it is a good dataset for training a CNN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ImageNet dataset is good for transfer learning because it is large and contains many classes, but the exact number of classes or images-per-class is not critical.
ImageNet is a good choice for pre-training because of its size, but not because of any particular characteristics of the data itself.
ImageNet is a good pre-training set because it is large, and that the quality of the pre-training is more important than any particular properties of the pre-training set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ImageNet’s success is due to the large number of images per class, and that the number of classes is not as important as commonly thought.
the success of ImageNet features is primarily a consequence of its large scale, rather than any particular properties of the dataset.
the ImageNet dataset, in its current form, is a good choice for pre-training deep features for transfer.
